brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.evidence: There are 3 cells in a row (piece:0,0,0, 1,0,0 and 2,0,0), each with a keyhole hanger on the same back face, so the rack can hang flat against a wall. The configurator doesn't rate how much load the hangers or wall screws can take.
There are 3 full-depth bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:2,0,0~hex-bin-full.
There are 3 hex-acc-keyhole hangers: accessory:0#0,0#1, accessory:0#1,0#1 and accessory:0#2,0#1, all in slot 1.

finish.summary: I built a wall-hung spice rack: three full hex cells in a row, each holding a full-depth bin, with one keyhole hanger per cell. The three hangers all sit on the same back face (slot 1), so the rack lifts onto screws already in the wall and drops into place. I capped the open faces with solid end caps and bolted the two joints between cells. That makes 20 parts, about 1554 g of filament and about 2145 minutes of printing. check_build reports no issues and the mesh-collision check came back clear. I didn't add props because the catalogue has no spice jars to put in the bins. The configurator only checks how the parts fit. It doesn't check how much weight the hangers or the wall screws can hold, so that's down to the material and the screws you choose.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
